question: The concept of 'Standard Urban Area (SUA)' was introduced in which census of India?
solution:
The Correct answer is __**Census 1971**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The concept of **Standard Urban Area (SUA)** was introduced during the **Census of 1971** in India.
 
• The purpose of defining SUAs was to identify and delineate urban areas with a specific set of criteria for better urban planning and management.
 
• An SUA typically includes a central city or town and its adjoining urban outgrowths that together form a continuous urban spread.
 
• This concept helps in understanding the urban agglomeration and the dynamics of urban growth and development.
 
• The criteria for defining an SUA may include population size, density, and the presence of urban characteristics such as infrastructure and economic activities.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Census 1961**__

 __
 
• The Census of 1961 introduced the concept of the "urban agglomeration," which refers to a continuous urban spread constituting a town and its adjoining urban outgrowths, or two or more physically contiguous towns together.
 
• This was a significant step towards understanding urbanization patterns in India.
 
 
 
• **Census 1951**__
 __
 
• The Census of 1951 was the first census conducted after India's independence in 1947.
 
• This census laid the foundation for the modern census operations in India, introducing several new methodologies and classifications.
 
 
 
• **Census 1981**__
 
 
• The Census of 1981 further refined the classifications and definitions of urban and rural areas, building upon the concepts introduced in previous censuses.
 
• This census also saw the introduction of computer-based data processing, which improved the accuracy and speed of data analysis.
